name_reason: Follows fd2_<domain>_<descriptor> convention and accurately describes the role: the top-level dispatcher that applies an item/spell USE effect by reading the item's K1 effect_code and routing to the right handler. No Ghidra address residue. Caller context (fd2_execute_ai_item_use AI side, fd2_item_command_menu_dispatch player side) confirms it is the single commit point for use-effects.
purpose: Top-level dispatcher that applies an item/spell USE effect: reads the item entry's K1 effect_code (+0xD) and K2/K3 effect_param (u16 @ +0xE), routes to the matching heal/cure/buff/inflict/stat-up/attack-spell handler, optionally consumes the inventory slot, then finalizes with XP reset and death/drop processing.
logic_summary: Preloads status-effect SFX bank, zeroes the AoE/fx-queue counter, looks up item_id from the caster's inventory slot and fetches its item-effect entry. effect_param = u16 @+0xE, effect_code = u8 @+0xD (K1). A long if/else-if chain dispatches on effect_code: 5/0xD group HP heal (5 also consumes); 6/7 status cure (then projectile-paths if any target hit, then consume); 8/9/0xA/0x11/0x12 permanent stat-up via fd2_apply_item_stat_modifier_with_anim with per-code field offset+anim idx; 0xB inline MP-restore loop (miss if mp_max==0 else heal+award XP+damage number) then consume; 0xC speed boost; 0xE/0x16 status inflict; 0xF DP boost; 0x10 AP boost; 0x13 stat-up to field 0x3B that saves and restores movement_order (animation-only, non-persistent); 0x14/0x18 inline attack-spell loop (calc_magic_damage -> miss or damage number glyph 0x5E); 0x15 fd2_apply_attack_spell_damage; 0x17 fd2_cast_spell_17_complex. Finale (all paths): pending_xp_credit=0, play+free status SFX, collect pending death drops into a stack buffer, play death animation + mark dead, process battle drop entries.
signature: void fd2_apply_use_effect_dispatch(uint32 caster_idx, uint32 inv_slot, uint32 target_count, uint32 p_target_array)

params.name: caster_idx
params.semantics: Runtime_char index of the unit using the item/spell (the caster). Passed straight to every dispatched handler and to fd2_get_inventory_slot_item_id / fd2_remove_inventory_slot_at / fd2_process_battle_drop_entries.
params.reason: Accurate, no address residue; matches caller usage.

params.name: inv_slot
params.semantics: Inventory slot to read the item from and (for consumable codes 5/6/7/0xB and the stat-scroll path) to remove after use.

params.name: target_count
params.semantics: Number of target runtime_char indices in p_target_array; loop bound for per-target effect loops.

params.name: p_target_array
params.semantics: Pointer (held as uint32) to a byte array of target runtime_char indices, length target_count. Indexed as a byte array in the inline loops and passed through to the dispatched handlers.
params.reason: Accurate descriptor with p_ prefix, no address residue. (Note: Ghidra's raw decompile mislabels this 4th param 'caster_idx'; the src name is the correct one.)

returns.semantics: No return value; effects are applied via side effects on runtime_char array, inventory, animation/SFX, and battle drop state.

notes: src comment block (spelleff.c lines 10-16) is already concise and correct (effect codes 5-0x18, finalizes with XP reset + death/drop processing); kept as-is per 'src concise+correct, not byte-identical to plate'. Ghidra plate is detailed and fully consistent with the decompilation and src; left unchanged. item_entry K1=effect_code@+0xD, K2/K3=effect_param u16@+0xE confirmed via fd2-knowledge struct item_entry (TY AP AP HT HT DP DP EV EV S1 S2 R1 R2 K1...). Code 0x13 save/restore of movement_order is intentional (animation-only stat bump), not a bug. No logic touched.
